title: Menubar apps each copy what arca_swift could carry: the masthead's two macOS 27 workarounds, the XCTest-host check, and a single-instance guard
body:
hv's ruling of 25 Oct 2026 in Conflab (ruling 3 in ST0125's design), relayed by conflab-vc and filed by conflab-ic: Menuz's macOS 27 workarounds go into arca_swift through an issue, so that no adopter copies them, and Conflab copies what it needs, with a pointer here, only if arca_swift has not shipped them by its cut. conflab-vc's routing of the same day, by analogy and open to hv's overrule, adds the XCTest-host check and a single-instance guard (Conflab's ST0125/WP-07).

**What adopters copy today:**
- **The row's image on macOS 27.** macOS 27 draws a menu item's image only when the item asks for it: the default visibility is automatic, and automatic drew no image in the masthead row. Menuz asks for `.visible` (raw value 1 in NSMenuItem.h) by key, once the item responds to `setPreferredImageVisibility:`, because the property is new in the macOS 27 SDK and a named reference does not compile against an older SDK, even inside `if #available` (Utilz `native/macos/Menuz/Menuz/Services/Masthead.swift`, `drawsImage(_:)`; Utilz issue 0073, `18e13a7f`). Gtools' `GtoolsApp.drawsImage` does the same (15 Sep 2026).
- **The app's icon in the row.** `MastheadRow` draws `NSApp.applicationIconImage`, whose AppKit default drew nothing in Menuz's row on macOS 27. Menuz sets it before it makes the row, from the icon file the bundle's `CFBundleIconFile` names, read by URL rather than by name, which can resolve through the Assets.xcassets folder to the default again (`setAppIcon(bundle:)`, `8a750cca`). Gtools.app and this package's example set an explicit bitmap, and draw theirs.
- **The XCTest-host check.** xcodebuild hosts an app's tests in the app, so the app's whole launch path runs in every test session: in Conflab's, a bridge server on a fixed port, the daemon's LaunchAgent, a status item and a global hotkey. Menuz's `AppDelegate.isTestHost(_:)` reads `XCTestConfigurationFilePath`, which xcodebuild sets in the host and a launch at login or by `open` does not, and its `applicationDidFinishLaunching` and `applicationWillTerminate` return at once when it holds (Utilz `MenuzApp.swift`, from Gtools' gtools#0050, pinned by `MenuzTests/TestHostTests.swift`). Gtools and Menuz carry a copy each, and Conflab takes a third now, with a pointer here.
- **A single-instance guard.** No adopter has one. On 25 Oct 2026 hv had two copies of Conflab's menubar app running, one of them on a binary since replaced on disk. `LSMultipleInstancesProhibited` is the wrong tool, because it would refuse xcodebuild's host beside a person's copy. Conflab's design: a runtime check at the top of the launch path, after the test-host check and before any side effect, where the running copy wins and a second launch activates it and exits, the macOS convention. Replacing an older running build is an install or swap step's job, not the guard's.

**Who it hits:** every estate menubar app: Gtools.app, menuz, Intent.app and Conflab.app.

**The ask:** arca_swift carries each of them, so that adopters stop copying them: the two masthead fixes inside `MastheadRow` or the call that makes it, and the test-host check and the guard as one launch-time call that an adopter's `applicationDidFinishLaunching` makes first. Each adopter's copy carries a pointer to this issue and goes once arca_swift ships its replacement.

**Size:** S.
